equivalents.note: The Tibetan has rab 'dred, 'very slippery', describing the two sides as slippery rather than naming mud, and the comment (cp.05.m2) likewise has shin tu 'dred pa.
The Tibetan dbus na 'dug gnas med, 'in the middle there is no place to stay', gives the sense of having nowhere to stand rather than a word for the bottom or footing.

The Tibetan reads gzong gnyis, 'two chisels', taking ādaa as 'two' (as if dvaya, without the negative of advaya) and attaching it to the tool, with diṭi apparently rendered by brtan par, 'firmly' (compare Munidatta's dṛḍhaṃ karoti in cp.05.m4).
The Sanskrit sentence with dhruvapadena closes cp.05.m2, but the Tibetan opens cp.05.m3 with it, transcribing only the cue dhru and translating pada as rkang pa, 'verse'.
In bzhi pa'i dga' ba, 'the fourth joy', for caturthānanda, in the sentence that the Sanskrit places at the end of cp.05.m2 and the Tibetan at the head of cp.05.m3.
Here rang bzhin, which the same segment also uses for prakṛti (rang bzhin gyi skyon), renders svarūpa word for word in tshad ma'i rang bzhin, 'the nature of the measure', for pramāṇasvarūpa.
The Tibetan recasts 'it has no form by its own nature' (svarūpeṇa nāsti rūpam) as rang bzhin gyis med pa'i gzugs, 'form without intrinsic nature', the usual phrase for niḥsvabhāva.
The Tibetan has bla ma'i drin gyis, 'by the guru's grace', where the Sanskrit has gurusampradāyāt, 'from the guru's lineage'.
Here the Tibetan has gsal snang, 'clear appearance', for the three appearances, where cp.05.m2 and cp.05.m5 have snang ba.
The Tibetan has rmongs pa chen po'i rtsa, 'the channel of great delusion', for mahāmohanadyāḥ, 'the river of great delusion', apparently reading nāḍī, 'channel', for nadī.

questions: bodhi (cp.05.4b): not matched. The Tibetan nye bar bdog pas ring du 'gro bar ma byed cig, 'since it is present close by, do not go far', has no word for awakening: either the subject is left unstated or bohi was read as something else (possibly a verb of being, rendered by bdog, though this is a guess). The byang chub of cp.05.5b (bla med byang chub) stands where the Bengali has anuttarasāmī, 'unsurpassed lord', so it is not the equivalent of bohi either.

samsara (cp.05.m3): not matched. For saṃsārasamudrasya pāraṃ the Tibetan has only rgya mtsho'i pha rol tu, 'to the far shore of the ocean', with no word for saṃsāra; the term is already matched in cp.05.m5 ('khor ba'i rgya mtsho).

p-jina (cp.05.m5): not matched. Where the Sanskrit has saṃkramaṃ jinasya sattvānāṃ, the Tibetan reads zam pa ste skye bo sems pa rnams, 'the bridge, for people, beings', with no word for the Jina; skye bo may reflect a reading janasya, 'of people', for jinasya (and sems pa may stand for sems can), but it does not render the name, so it is not offered as an equivalent.

dharma and sahajananda (cp.05.m6): not matched. The Tibetan compresses siddhācāryopadeśapāramparyeṇānuttaradharmasvāminam āha — pṛcchatheti | ataeva sahajānandopadeśaṃ jānāmy ahaṃ niścitam into grub pa'i slob dpon gyi man ngag bdag gis nges par shes so, 'I know for certain the instruction of the siddha master', with nothing for 'the lord of the unsurpassed Dharma', the call to ask, or innate joy.

thaha (cp.05.m2): matched only in the verse line (cp.05.1b). In the comment, where the Sanskrit has madhye tasyāḥ thāhaṃ, the Tibetan has no word for footing and reads instead rang bzhin gyi skyon gyi 'dam gyis ma gos pa dbu ma'i don la bdag nyid de, 'unstained by the mud of the faults of nature, its nature is the sense of the middle', applying the mud to the middle rather than to the banks.
